Get started with easyNIS

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

This workflow uses invented inpatient discharges from nis_example(). In a study, use the path to your converted annual Parquet files and supply your own diagnosis definitions and eligibility rules.

Open, project, and flag

Choose the study years in nis_open(). Select the columns needed for the analysis, keeping the design fields and the diagnosis slots used by the flag. The query stays in DuckDB. The diagnosis flag checks every slot by default.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  dplyr::select(nis_vars_design(), nis_vars_dx(), AGE, FEMALE, LOS, DIED, DISPUNIFORM) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50") |>
  nis_outcomes() |>
  dplyr::mutate(adult = AGE >= 18)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp2JR7WX/duckdb

nis_attrition(nis, adult = adult, by_year = TRUE, .design = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 8
#>    YEAR  step criterion             n_unweighted n_dropped_unweighted n_weighted
#>   <int> <int> <chr>                        <int>                <int>      <dbl>
#> 1  2020     0 Valid design dischar…           96                   NA       114.
#> 2  2020     1 adult                           96                    0       114.
#> 3  2019     0 Valid design dischar…           96                   NA       114.
#> 4  2019     1 adult                           96                    0       114.
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_dropped_weighted <dbl>, pct_retained <dbl>

nis_vars_design() keeps YEAR, HOSP_NIS, NIS_STRATUM, DISCWT and, when present, DQTR. If a prior selection removed one of the four required fields, nis_design() reports the missing field. See Defining cohorts for principal diagnoses, exclusions, procedure flags, and code-system choices.

Estimate within the adult domain

Pass the eligibility flag to cohort so the variance calculation can account for sampled hospital-years with no eligible discharges. keep limits what the design brings into R, and the design labels retained HCUP fields. The flag groups compare adult discharges with and without a matching diagnosis.

design <- nis |>
  nis_design(cohort = adult, keep = c(heart_failure, AGE, FEMALE, los_days, in_hospital_death))
#> Cohort: 192 discharges; weighted N 228.8; 24 hospitals across 2 years.

estimates <- design |>
  dplyr::group_by(heart_failure) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    discharges = srvyr::survey_total(),
    mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(los_days, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

This estimates totals across both study years. Use annualize = TRUE for average annual totals when each included year represents a whole year. For annual estimates, keep the original weights and group by YEAR. See Survey design and weighting for pooling and coverage.

Make a table and fit a model

Use the same design for the descriptive table and regression. The model adjusts for age, sex, and year in this invented example. Review the model sample and missingness when reporting a real analysis.

table_one <- design |>
  gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(by = heart_failure, include = c(AGE, FEMALE, los_days, in_hospital_death))
nis_suppress(table_one)
Characteristic TRUE
N = 1251,2 		FALSE
N = 1041,2
Age, years 59 (41, 76) 65 (49, 77)
Sex of patient 62 (50%) 52 (50%)
los_days 6.0 (3.0, 9.0) 5.0 (2.0, 8.0)
in_hospital_death ≤10 ≤10
1 Median (Q1, Q3); n (%)
2 Statistics based on unweighted n ≤10 are marked ≤10; cells contributed by fewer than two distinct year-scoped hospitals are marked '<2 hospitals', regardless of count. The discharge-count mask takes precedence when both rules apply. Dichotomous rows with a protected complement are marked 'Masked' when the displayed event passes both rules. Other derivable cells are not masked; review tables for other derivable cells before sharing under the HCUP Data Use Agreement. 
fit <- survey::svyglm(
  in_hospital_death ~ heart_failure + AGE + FEMALE + factor(YEAR),
  design = design,
  family = quasibinomial()
)

Review disclosure before exporting

The table above masks statistics using corresponding unweighted counts and hospital support. For a data-frame summary, attach those counts explicitly. This fixture has recorded LOS for every discharge. With missing LOS, use counts for the records contributing to that mean.

reviewed <- estimates |>
  dplyr::left_join(nis_cell_counts(design, by = heart_failure), by = "heart_failure") |>
  nis_suppress(
    count_col = "n",
    hospital_col = "hospitals",
    weighted_cols = c("discharges", "discharges_se", "mean_los", "mean_los_se")
  )
reviewed
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   heart_failure discharges discharges_se    mean_los mean_los_se n     hospitals
#>   <lgl>         <chr>      <chr>            <chr>    <chr>       <chr> <chr>    
#> 1 FALSE         104        19.9077874210069 5.38076… 0.27278462… 84    24       
#> 2 TRUE          124.8      17.3481987537612 5.66346… 0.22899117… 108   18

Review disclosure across tables, models, and related totals before sharing. Keep work in a private directory. See Disclosure and suppression.

utils::write.csv(reviewed, "discharges-reviewed.csv", row.names = FALSE)

Project before collecting

When a step needs a data frame, put select() before collect() so DuckDB can read the requested columns from Parquet. In a Windows benchmark, fresh R 4.6.1 processes with DuckDB 1.5.2 selected the same seven columns from 480,000 invented rows and 188 source columns. Peak process commit was 206 MiB with projection before collection and 1,379 MiB with projection after collection. The difference measures one synthetic workload. Peak memory depends on the data, query, and system.

To reproduce the measurement from the easyNIS source directory on Windows, install the package and run these commands with a new scratch directory.

Rscript --vanilla tools/benchmark-column-projection.R prepare local/loop/wide-invented
Rscript --vanilla tools/benchmark-column-projection.R early local/loop/wide-invented
Rscript --vanilla tools/benchmark-column-projection.R late local/loop/wide-invented
